snippet.title: The Murder of Saudi Arabia’s King | ASSASSINS
snippet.description:
In 1975 a young Saudi prince entered the royal palace and shot dead the king, Faisal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud. 

The killing was both personal and political, linked to the death of a brother, the tension between tradition and modernisation, and the introduction of television to the desert kingdom. Subscribe: https://ab.co/3yqPOZ5

snippet.title: Oil and gas project that promised Timor-Leste riches hasn't delivered | 7.30
snippet.description:
When he visited Timor-Leste last week, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he brought good news on the long-stalled Greater Sunrise oil and gas project.

But the stalemate over the operation continues.

Reporter Nick Sas travelled to the small village of Suai, where the promised riches of oil and gas have not materialised.

snippet.title: New documents from the Epstein files cause shockwaves around the world | 7.30
snippet.description:
Millions more documents relating to the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein were released by the US Department of Justice last week and observers are still poring over them.

The story the files tell is one of base corruption that stains all it touches. But Epstein was also a notorious liar and blackmailer, so the fact that he mentioned someone in his communications doesn't mean that they were part of his network.

7.30’s Alysia Thomas Sam reports.
